text:
Liam: Small but annoying onboarding bug: sample apps set REDWOOD_KEY and the SDK helpers prefer REDWOOD_API_KEY_ORG. Partners get 401s.

Priya: We need a single priority agreed and a tiny helper across SDKs. Suggest order: 1) explicit key arg, 2) REDWOOD_API_KEY_PROJECT, 3) REDWOOD_API_KEY_ORG, 4) REDWOOD_API_KEY.

Grace: Agree. For rotation: CLI always re-reads env. SDKs should 1) read on construct, 2) on first 401 re-read once and retry. Avoid watchers or long polling.

Liam: Can we export resolveApiKey() in each SDK so sample apps call that instead of copying logic? Then docs reference one canonical behavior.

Priya: yes. Example Node helper:
```js
function resolveApiKey(explicitKey){
  return explicitKey || process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY_PROJECT || process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY_ORG || process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY;
}
// on 401: call resolveApiKey() again and retry once
```

Grace: CLI UX: add `redwood auth status` that prints which env var was chosen (not the secret) and warn if legacy REDWOOD_API_KEY is used alongside project key.

Ops-bot: Created ticket DX-4275 "SDK resolveApiKey helper + env var priority" and linked this thread.

Liam: Action items: Priya write a short RFC + grep for legacy names (due Tue). Grace open CLI PR for `auth status` (WIP). I'll update quickstart sample to use resolveApiKey().

Priya: Also add a note for CI: GH Actions example `env: REDWOOD_API_KEY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY_PROJECT }}` and Docker note: avoid building secrets into images.

Liam: Great, thanks — keeping this small should remove a lot of partner friction.
